quiz.title: Module 2 — Tuesday — Creating Powerful Typography
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers the first video's techniques — size contrast, the heading-to-body ratio, skipping a font weight, aligning to a grid, using lines and shapes to group text, and justified alignment — and the second video's outlined text and gradient overlay in Photoshop.

questions.prompt: According to the first video, what is the main purpose of creating a clear difference between text sizes in a design?
options: To make every line of text look identical
To ensure the design contains as much text as possible
To establish visual hierarchy and make the text easier to organize
To eliminate the need for font-weight variations
questions.explanation: Size is the plainest signal of importance. A clear jump between sizes tells the viewer what to read first and how the content is ordered.

questions.prompt: In the first video, a designer uses a heading size of 75 points and divides it by 5 to determine the body text size. What is the resulting body text size?
options: 10 points
15 points
25 points
35 points
questions.explanation: 75 ÷ 5 = 15. Dividing the heading size gives the body text a fixed, deliberate proportion rather than an arbitrary one.

questions.prompt: Why does the first video recommend skipping a font weight when creating contrast between text?
options: It creates a more noticeable visual difference between text elements
It makes every text element appear the same thickness
It removes the need to consider text size
It ensures that all text is displayed in italics
questions.explanation: Neighbouring weights such as regular and medium are too close to read as a deliberate contrast. Skipping one makes the difference obvious at a glance.

questions.prompt: According to the first video, what is a major benefit of aligning text consistently with a grid line?
options: It allows designers to use unlimited fonts
It makes every paragraph perfectly justified
It removes the need for spacing between text elements
It creates a cleaner, more organized design that is easier to read
questions.explanation: A shared grid line holds the elements in a fixed relationship, so the layout reads as organised rather than loosely scattered.

questions.prompt: How can lines and shapes help improve the organization of typography in a design?
options: By making every text element the same size
By visually separating and grouping related text elements
By replacing all headings with decorative symbols
By forcing every paragraph into the center of the layout
questions.explanation: A rule or shape draws a boundary. It tells the viewer which pieces of text belong together and where one group ends and the next begins.

questions.prompt: According to the first video, why should designers avoid forcing paragraphs into justified alignment when it creates unwanted gaps?
options: Justified text cannot be used in graphic design
It makes the font weight too heavy
Large or awkward spaces can disrupt the natural reading flow
It prevents designers from using a grid
questions.explanation: Justification stretches the spaces between words to fill the line. When the gap grows large, the eye catches on the holes and the reading rhythm breaks.

questions.prompt: In the second video, what is the purpose of duplicating a text layer, setting its fill opacity to zero, and adding a white stroke?
options: To create an outlined version of the text that can be positioned behind the main text
To permanently remove the text from the design
To convert the text into a background image
To automatically correct the spacing between paragraphs
questions.explanation: Zero fill hides the letter bodies while the stroke keeps the outline. Placed behind the original, it makes an outlined double that reads as a deliberate framing device.

questions.prompt: After combining the text groups in Photoshop, which effect does the second video apply to give the typography design a colored appearance?
options: Gaussian Blur
Drop Shadow
Motion Blur
Gradient Overlay
questions.explanation: A Gradient Overlay maps a colour blend across everything in the layer, so the combined text takes on a single coloured treatment at once.
